elements.element: Services performed in a professional manner
elements.evidence: Clause addresses only that "each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation"; no services standard stated.

elements.element: Services performed in a workmanlike manner
elements.evidence: No workmanlike standard anywhere in the redlined text.
"will materially conform to its documentation" — conformance is qualified by "materially".
"For ninety (90) days after delivery" — 90 days, not 12 months, and no software-specific period.

elements.element: 90-day services warranty period measured from performance/completion
elements.evidence: Only a Deliverable period "after delivery"; no services period.
Redline states only "Nothing in this Section limits ... the remedies in Sections 6.2 and 19.4"; no repair obligation stated.
No replacement remedy in the operative text.
Refund cut-off was deleted but no affirmative refund remedy was inserted.
No compliance-with-laws language in 19.2 as redlined.

"For ninety (90) days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform" — 90 days is present but is tied to Deliverables with a "materially" qualification rather than express software conformance to documentation.
No services warranty or 30-day period stated.
Only a cross-reference: "the remedies in Sections 6.2 and 19.4"; no repair/replace/refund duty in this clause.

offending_extra_words: Nothing in this Section limits the warranties in Section 19.1 or 19.3 or the remedies in Sections 6.2 and 19.4.
reasons: Locked level is preferred, but the redline changes only the duration (fifteen days to ninety (90) days) and leaves every other preferred element absent: no professional and workmanlike services standard, no 12-month software conformance period, no 90-day services period measured from performance, no repair/replace/refund remedies, no compliance-with-laws warranty and no malicious-code warranty.
The conformance obligation remains qualified as "materially conform to its documentation", which falls short of the required documentation conformance at either level.
Fallback also fails on material terms: no 30-day services warranty and no express repair, replace or refund remedy; the clause merely cross-references remedies elsewhere.

Minimality fails: deleting the cut-off sentence ("after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation") was sufficient; the added non-limitation boilerplate cross-referencing Sections 19.1, 19.3, 6.2 and 19.4 is unnecessary and imports dependencies on other sections.
Unrelated commercial terms and untouched sentences remain effective; no undefined term or contradiction introduced.
